name: Chamillionaire
hook: A Houston rapper whose 'Ridin'' won a Grammy, and who said Weird Al's parody of it proved it was the rap song of the year.

blurb.age13: Chamillionaire, born Hakeem Seriki in Washington, D.C., in 1979, moved to Houston, Texas, when he was four. He made an early album with his high-school classmate Paul Wall. His single 'Ridin'' (2006) went to number one in America and won a Grammy. He made his next album without swearing once. Later he became a technology investor.
blurb.adult: Born in Washington, D.C., in 1979 and raised in Houston's Acres Homes, Seriki recorded 'Get Ya Mind Correct' with Paul Wall before his solo debut 'The Sound of Revenge' (2005). 'Ridin'', featuring Krayzie Bone, reached number one on the Hot 100 and won the 2007 Grammy for Best Rap Performance by a Duo or Group. 'Ultimate Victory' (2007) contains no profanity from him. He has since worked in technology investment, including as entrepreneur in residence at Upfront Ventures from 2015.
